scenario: AITA: My friend sent me a screenshot of her grades, and I'm upset | The other day my friend texted me: "\[cramberrycat\], look, isn't it beautiful?" and sent me a screenshot of her grades: a column of straight A's. It was only this narrow strip, which means she must've taken the pains to crop the screenshot so only the grade letters showed up: no class names, percentages, or extra stuff. ​ I forgot exactly what I did. I know I was kind of surprised and irritated that she did this. (Who sends their friends screenshots of their grades? Is this a thing? If so, please fill me in.) Granted, we are on the nerdier side of friends and of course we talk about grades, but I felt like this was too much. I might've ignored her text for a few hours because I was afraid I might say something wrong, which would probably mark me as the A-hole, but I can't remember if I did. ​ Some time after she had already sent the screenshot, she texted me "Sorry" so I'm not sure, maybe she realized how I might feel and apologized for crossing some sort of line? (If there is, in fact, such a line?) I eventually replied, "Truly a sight to behold", which was deliberate in that it did not reflect my true feelings at all. ​ But in terms of my feelings, and my non-verbal reaction, AITA? Was I wrong to be so upset by it? I just felt it was kind of annoying and unnecessary. I'm not sure if she did it with the intention of hurting me or making me jealous; I'm less open about my grades than she is, because she gets consistent high A's on tests while I get B+'s to low A's, although formerly I was a high A's student. I just feel like I'm being too sensitive or overanalyzing it, which has been the case many a time in the past.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was wrong to be upset when my friend sent me a screenshot of her grades. She sent me a cropped screenshot showing only straight A's, and I felt annoyed and unnecessary. I'm not sure if she did this to make me jealous or if it was just her being proud of her achievements. I also wonder if it's normal for friends to share their grades like that. I ended up ignoring her texts for a few hours and then replied with "Truly a sight to behold," which didn't really reflect how I felt. Now I'm questioning if I was too sensitive or overreacting. First, I need to understand why I felt upset. Maybe it's because I'm not as open about my grades as she is. I used to get high A's, but now I get B+'s to low A's. So, seeing her straight A's might have triggered some insecurities or feelings of inadequacy. But is that a valid reason to be upset? Or should I just be happy for her? On the other hand, I think about whether it's appropriate for her to send such a screenshot. I mean, grades are personal, and not everyone shares them openly. Maybe she didn't realize that sending this could make me feel bad. Or maybe she did it innocently, just to share her success. I'm not sure. I also wonder about the cropped screenshot. She went to the effort to crop it so that only the grades showed, no class names or percentages. That seems intentional. Maybe she wanted to highlight her achievements without giving too much detail. But why would she do that? Is it to show off, or is it just her way of sharing good news? I'm also thinking about how I responded. I ignored her for a few hours and then gave a non-committal reply. That might have made her feel bad, especially since she later apologized. Maybe I should have communicated my feelings more openly instead of bottling them up. Another thing to consider is whether this is a common thing among friends. Do people usually share their grades like that? I don't recall my other friends doing this, so maybe it's not a typical behavior. If that's the case, then her action might have crossed a line without her realizing it. I also need to reflect on my own behavior. Did I overreact? Am I being too sensitive? I know I tend to overanalyze situations, so maybe this is just another instance of that. But at the same time, my feelings are valid, and it's okay to feel upset if something affects me negatively. In the end, I think the key is communication. If I feel upset, I should talk to her about it instead of ignoring her or giving a fake response. That way, we can understand each other's perspectives and avoid misunderstandings in the future. So, to sum up, I was upset because seeing her straight A's triggered some insecurities, and her cropped screenshot seemed intentional. I overreacted by ignoring her and giving a non-genuine reply. It might have been better to communicate my feelings openly to avoid further issues.
